_note: Case 2 — a new brand in a DIFFERENT industry (outdoor gear / apparel, not edtech). Pair with data/generic_outdoor_gear.json as its competitor corpus — there is no existing generic file for this industry, so a new one was written. Illustrative text, not copied from any live brand.

assets.name: TrailForge
assets.mission: Build outdoor equipment good enough that repair, not replacement, is the default choice.
assets.vision: A world where 'gear graveyard' stops being a real category on landfill maps.
assets.values: If it breaks before ten years, we redesign it, we don't remarket it. We publish our repair rates in public. Repair is a feature, not a favor we grant reluctantly. We would rather sell you one jacket in a decade than four.
assets.about: We started in a garage fixing gear that other companies wouldn't repair under warranty. After a few years of fixing other people's design mistakes for free, we decided to stop being generous and start being the ones who design it properly in the first place.
assets.founder_story: One of us used to run warranty claims for a large outdoor brand and got tired of approving replacements for the same broken zipper pull, year after year, on a jacket that was otherwise fine. We now sell that same jacket with a zipper pull you can replace yourself with a coin.
homepage: Ten-year warranty. We mean it literally, not as a marketing number.
Every seam, zipper and buckle is field-replaceable. We sell the parts, not just the jacket.
Built by people who used to approve your warranty claims somewhere else.
product_page: The 3-layer shell is rated to 20,000mm and shipped with the spare zipper pull it will eventually need, because it will eventually need one.
We publish the failure point on every product page: where it wears first, and how long that takes under normal use.
No seasonal colorways. We make one version of each product and improve it once a year, in place.
cta: Buy the jacket you'll still be wearing in ten winters.
Send us the broken one. We'll tell you if it's worth fixing before you pay for shipping.
See the failure-rate data before you check out.
blog: We tore down our own five-year-old jacket next to a competitor's this-season model. Ours had less material fatigue at the seams. Full photos and pressure-test numbers inside.
Why we stopped doing seasonal colorways: it made customers replace gear that wasn't broken, and that's the opposite of what we're trying to do.
The real cost of a 'lifetime warranty' with a shrinking list of covered parts. We list our covered parts and don't shrink the list.
social: Someone sent us a photo of our jacket from 2016, still in rotation, patched twice. This is the whole business model in one photo.
Asked us for a discount code. We don't run those. Asked us for the repair guide instead — that one's free and always will be.
ad: A jacket that's still working in ten years costs less per year than one you replace every three.
We will tell you the exact hour count our zippers are rated for. Nobody else will.
job_post: You'll spend real time in the field pressure-testing gear before it ships, not just reading the spec sheet. If that sounds slow, this isn't the team for you.
We need someone who gets annoyed by a product roadmap built around a sales calendar instead of a wear-testing calendar.
support_doc: Every zipper, buckle and drawcord we sell is listed with a part number so you can replace it yourself without mailing the whole jacket back to us.
Repairs outside the warranty window are billed at cost of parts only — we do not mark up labor on gear we already sold you once.
case_study: A guiding company outfitted twelve guides in 2015; by 2024, all twelve jackets were still in active rotation with an average of 1.3 field repairs each, logged and shared with us.
testimonial: I mailed them a photo of a torn cuff expecting a sales pitch for a new jacket. They mailed me a $6 replacement cuff and instructions instead.
